newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Meyer sees modest recovery, "not unhappy" with Sfr.
newsitem.headline: Meyer sees modest recovery, "not unhappy" with Sfr.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) Chairman Hans Meyer said on Thursday the Swiss economy remained weak, but a modest recovery appeared to be in the offing next year.
One factor among many for the weakness in the economy was the strength of the Swiss franc on exchange markets.
Meyer said the SNB was "not unhappy" with the franc's recent decline. But he also said one should not assume the SNB was conducting a monetary policy solely aimed at currencies.
The SNB has eased its monetary policy in the past year.

"One result of this is that the value of the franc has corrected downwards. You can assume that we are not unhappy about this development, but without concluding that we are conducting a monetary policy aimed only at currencies," Meyer said.

The dollar rose on November 6 to 1.2850 Swiss francs, its highest level since mid-February 1995. The mark on November 6 also hit a peak of 84.32 Swiss centimes, its highest level since March 1995. With respect to the Swiss economy, Meyer said: "I would clearly say that today's economic situation is not good. It is poor."
There were signs the economy was picking up and added the monetary easing had created a good framework for this. But he added: "It will not be a quick recovery."

He said the reasons for the poor economy included overall economic weakness in Europe and the need to get Swiss public spending under control, as well as the strength of the Swiss franc. But he said there were a few positive elements, one being that "stagnation has taken place at a high level. In spite of everything the standard of living is high."
Meyer made his comments to a university business forum.
